items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: they put us together on his first tour without the Basie band. And we stayed together for about three years. And about four years we travelled together.

ctx.x: You travelled a lot with them?

Yes, in fact when Joe Williams left the Count Basie band, Basie’s office was my manager and they were managing Joe Williams too, so they put us together on his first tour without the Basie band. And we stayed together for about three years. And about four years we travelled together.

Before we get into that period where you became a leader and left Basie, the first time you left Basie after your long stay, I wanted to return to life on the road for a second and ask, logistically, how did you deal with the whole problem of segregation, of where you ate…you already talked about how you stayed in private homes, but how did you stop on the road with the bus and find a toilet, find a restaurant?

items.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I was the first band that he went on the road with when he left Basie. I had the band... And we went out together for a couple of years, two or three years.

ctx.x: It’s on its way. Is there any humorous or just really interesting stories you can share with us about either Basie or Joe Williams, the time together, that maybe we haven’t read in a book.
Well there’s not too much I could say about Joe because he wasn’t with the band that I was with. I was with the original Count Basie band.
His hit came after your tenure — that “Every Day.”

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: Basie put the both of us together, Joe Williams... Joe Williams and myself... we were very fortunate, because the first date together was at Storeyville

ctx.x: From '57 -- well, then, you know, when Joe Williams left Basie, Will Alexander was handling me and Basie put the both of us together, Joe Williams.

items.title: Joe Williams interviewed by Leslie Gourse, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Harry “Sweets” Edison... [INTERVIEWEE] Yup, yup, yup, yup, yup.

ctx.x: Harry “Sweets” Edison, and I like that Bohanon, the trombonist you worked with, and so many of them. I mean I love them. Jimmy Jones and everyone.
Yup, yup, yup, yup, yup. Hank Jones, Jimmy Jones, Osie Johnson, Milt Hinton, Kenny Burrell, oh boy, Romeo Penque, Harold Lookofsky. Really all these wonderful — Zoot Sims, Frank Foster, and —
